<!-- Generated by `node scripts/docs-reference.mjs`. Do not edit. -->

A project is more than the audio: it is the tracks, clips, effects, markers and history. Saving keeps all of that in the browser’s local project library on this computer, where it can be reopened from the File menu. Soundscaper also saves as you go, so this is mostly a way to be sure.

:::note[Coming from Audacity?]
This is Audacity's **File → Save Project**. The names below are Soundscaper's own, which sometimes differ.
:::

## Steps

1. Open Soundscaper. A new, empty project is ready as soon as the editor loads.
2. Choose **File → Import audio** and pick your recording. This lesson uses `lesson-music-loop.wav`. The file lands as a clip on its own track.
3. Choose **File → Save project**. The save indicator in the status bar shows the project is saved.

## Tips

- To move a project to another computer or keep a copy outside the browser, see [Move a project between computers](/lessons/move-a-project-between-computers/).
- An audio export is a listening copy, not a project. Keep the project if you may edit again.

## About this lesson

Every step on this page is replayed against each build of Soundscaper by the browser suite (`tests/browser/soundscaper-lessons.spec.js`). If a menu entry, field or button stops matching, the build fails until the lesson is corrected, so the steps you read are the steps the editor accepts.
